I’ll locate where prompt versions add internal tags, copy the caller’s dictionary before that happens, and add a regression test. I’ll use the repository’s Python style skill for the change.
The mutation happens in the `PromptVersion` constructor: it adds internal tags directly to any nonempty dictionary it receives. I’ll copy that dictionary first and test that reusing it preserves both versions’ templates and keeps the first version’s model configuration out of the second.
Updated `PromptVersion` to copy caller-provided tags before adding internal entries, preventing mutations and leakage between versions.

Added regression coverage for text/chat templates and empty/custom tags, including model configuration isolation.

All 56 tests in `tests/entities/test_prompt.py` passed; pytest then hit a sandbox permission error in its summary hook. No dependencies installed.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("template", ["Hello {{name}}", [{"role": "user", "content": "{{name}}"}]])
+def test_prompt_initialization_does_not_mutate_tags(tags, template):
+    original_tags = tags.copy()
+    first = PromptVersion(
+        name="my_prompt",
+        version=1,
+        template=template,
+        tags=tags,
+        model_config={"temperature": 0.7},
+    )
+    assert tags == original_tags
+
+    second = PromptVersion(name="my_prompt", version=2, template="Hi!", tags=tags)
+    assert tags == original_tags
+    assert first.tags == original_tags
+    assert second.tags == original_tags
+    assert first.template == template
+    assert second.template == "Hi!"
+    assert first.model_config == {"temperature": 0.7}
+    assert second.model_config is None
